findings.title: Unsuccessful selection publication is accepted as a frozen selection and admits evaluator progression
locations: training/holistic_migration/tests/test_evaluate.py:37-87 (healthy selection/tamper controls omit failed selection publication disposition)
findings.mechanism: The producer links selection.json and its final digest readback raises. The evaluator-owned publisher attempts rollback, which raises an ordinary PermissionError; the primary is correctly preserved and _training_failure successfully persists failure.json. Once transient faults clear, frozen_selection checks the residual success bytes and their bound files/history but does not distinguish unsuccessful selection publication from successful freezing followed by later report failure. _evaluate calls this consumer and then permits _reserve; there is no intermediate failed-selection denial.
findings.observed: Worker stage15 and independent parent each reached one behavioral failure/zero errors. The reviewer phase-sensitive two-case probe independently reached the actual evaluator reservation boundary from the failed selection; a sentinel stopped before mkdir/start/native checkpoint/test access. Original error identity, retained selection+pending+failure, unchanged frozen-run bytes, and absent evaluation output were asserted. The failed-publication expected-denial assertion failed.
findings.healthy_control: The paired reviewer control fails metrics only after _publish_json(selection.json) returns successfully. That valid selection plus failure.json remains consumable and reaches the same intercepted evaluator admission boundary; this control PASSED as required by task-d-brief.md:81. A blanket failure.json rejection at frozen_selection would break this intentional behavior.
findings.materiality: High-priority scientific workflow/gating correctness. Failed final readback is promoted to a frozen prerequisite for separate held-out evaluation even though durable failure persistence succeeded. No crash, hostile writer, permanent media loss, or simultaneous rollback-and-failure-persistence failure is required. The fault exists in protected code outside the completed trainer-only repair authority, but still belongs to the original eight-path Task D acceptance boundary.
non_claims: No actual-source training, real proof, held-out data read/inference, synthetic-to-real CLI bypass, model activation or security exploit was demonstrated.
This is not a reopening of D-R1-001/D-R2-001 evaluator-completion mechanisms or D-R3-001 tiny-proof gate.
